question.text: What is 'self-front-running' as identified by the Supreme Court in the Kanaiyalal Patel case?

answer.text: Transactions where the owner or purchaser of a block trade engages in offsetting futures or options transactions as a means of hedging against price fluctuations caused by the block transaction
A trader placing multiple orders in rapid succession ahead of their own limit orders
An intermediary trading ahead of its own proprietary orders
An individual front-running their own family members' orders

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook page 151, self-front-running, as identified by the Supreme Court, is when the owner or purchaser of a block trade himself engages in offsetting futures or options transactions as a means of hedging against price fluctuations caused by the block transaction. The Trap: Option C describes a proprietary-trading conflict where the intermediary trades ahead of its own proprietary orders, which is not the self-front-running concept defined in the case. Options B and D describe unrelated order-placement patterns. Note: The hallmark of self-front-running is the use of offsetting derivatives by the block-trade owner/purchaser to hedge the price impact of that very block trade.
